output.name: Lathesk
output.myth: Ennu the Kite-Wright found a plank on the north beach, split down its length where a boat broke on the rocks. His youngest sister wanted to fly, and there was no cloth fit for it, so he lashed the wood into a frame and stretched sailcloth across it, one knot at each corner. The wind took it up. She screamed with joy and would not give back the string. Hesk watched from the pole and said nothing, but she counted the four knots on her fingers, and the Counting Hands keep her tally. When the girl grew old and went aloft herself, Ennu would not burn the frame, and it would not burn anyway. So he hung it in the Spindle on a cord of Hesk's own thread, where no gale can reach it. Out west, the Drop Spindle still turns after the cut end. Each winter Tavo the Gale rattles the house-poles, and the frame stays put. Mothers tie a scrap of red cloth to the knot at its foot before a child first flies, so the wind knows whose it is.
output.finding: Find the Drop Spindle out in the west, then look one hand-span (about 20°) due east of it, where the Driftwood Frame hangs in the Spindle.
